# `Q-3-53` — Figure Not Supported in ANSI Format

> Figure elements cannot be rendered in ANSI terminal output.

## What this means

A figure is an image (or a group of images) with an attached
caption. The ANSI writer (used when rendering to a terminal)
does not render figures: a terminal cannot display the image,
and printing only the caption would lose the relationship
between caption and content.

## Why this happens

Your document contains a figure block — either a Pandoc-style
`![caption](path)` paragraph promoted to a figure, or an
explicit `::: figure` fenced div — and you rendered to ANSI
output.

## How to fix

Render to a different format. If you do want a terminal-friendly
view that mentions the figure, render to markdown (`--to qmd`)
or strip the figures with a filter before sending the AST to the
ANSI writer.

## Related

- `Q-3-50`, `Q-3-51`, `Q-3-52`, `Q-3-54`, `Q-3-55` — other
  block types the ANSI writer does not yet support.
